SELECTED_INDEX: 3
CONFIDENCE: 0.65
EXPLANATION: A very strong band at 2234 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a nitrile ν(C≡N), which candidate 3 contains. The two strong bands at 1654 and 1634 cm⁻¹ are consistent with an amide carbonyl (amide I) and a C=C stretch, respectively; candidate 3 has an amide and a cumulated C=C unit. CH stretches at 2913–2956 cm⁻¹ and multiple CH bending bands match an aliphatic framework. Candidates 2, 4, and 5 (azides) lack a nitrile and would place ν(N₃) lower (~2100–2160 cm⁻¹). Candidate 1 (aldehyde) and 6 (ester) would show a strong C=O near 1720–1740 cm⁻¹, which is absent. Alkyne-only candidates (7–10) do not explain a 2234 cm⁻¹ band. Hence 3 best fits the Raman evidence.
